excerpt: Socrates left no writings; his method of relentless questioning (elenchus) to expose contradictions was recorded by Plato. Executed in 399 BC for 'corrupting the youth.'
Plato's dialogue on justice and the ideal state, containing the Allegory of the Cave and the theory of Forms.
Aristotle's inquiry into virtue, happiness (eudaimonia), and the golden mean between extremes.
Private Stoic reflections of the Roman emperor on duty, mortality, and control over one's own judgments.
Aquinas' synthesis of Aristotelian philosophy with Christian theology, including his Five Ways arguing for God's existence.
Founding text of modern philosophy. 'Cogito, ergo sum' — I think, therefore I am — as the one indubitable truth.
Argues the mind is a blank slate (tabula rasa); all knowledge derives from experience. Foundational to empiricism and liberalism.
Radical empiricism and skepticism about causation and the self. 'Reason is, and ought only to be, the slave of the passions.'
Attempts to reconcile rationalism and empiricism, arguing the mind actively structures experience through categories like space and time.
Traces the dialectical development of consciousness toward absolute knowledge. Introduced the master–slave dialectic.
Critique of political economy analyzing capitalism, commodity fetishism, and the exploitation of labor.
Declares that 'God is dead' and introduces the Übermensch and eternal recurrence in a poetic, prophetic style.
With A. N. Whitehead, an attempt to derive all mathematics from logical axioms. A landmark of analytic philosophy.
Existentialist treatise on radical freedom and bad faith. 'Existence precedes essence' — we define ourselves through choices.
